title: Enhancing Students’ Learning Outcomes in Mathematics through Intelligent Tutoring Systems Based on Real-Time Feedback
extended_summary:
This study investigated whether an intelligent tutoring system (ITS) with automated real-time feedback improves students’ mathematical learning outcomes more than the same ITS without feedback. The focal outcome was students’ conceptual structure in mathematics, defined through the Structure of Observed Learning Outcomes (SLO) framework, especially in Measurement and Geometry. The authors aimed to address the limits of traditional assessment and delayed feedback by testing whether AI-supported, immediate diagnostic feedback could produce stronger learning gains.

The intervention was an AI-driven ITS that used a supervised machine learning decision tree model to classify students into SLO proficiency levels and then provide personalized instructional pathways. Students in the experimental condition received immediate textual or visual feedback and scaffolding when misconceptions were detected, while students in the control condition used the same platform and content but without automated feedback. Both groups completed pretest and posttest assessments using an open-ended diagnostic instrument with reported psychometric strength.

The study was conducted in Thailand at the Demonstration School of Khon Kaen University with Grade 7 gifted students in a specialized mathematics program. The study population included 120 students, with 78 systematically sampled and randomly assigned to experimental and control groups of 39 each. The context was a school-based mathematics learning environment focused on geometry-related content aligned to the Thai national curriculum.

Results showed significantly greater gains for students who used the ITS with real-time feedback. The experimental group improved from a mean of 1.90 to 3.54, compared with 1.90 to 2.85 in the control group, and achieved a higher progression percentage (84.83% vs. 61.54%). The reported between-group effect size was 0.73, indicating a meaningful positive effect. The authors conclude that ITS platforms with automated diagnostic feedback can substantially strengthen conceptual mathematics learning, though the pilot nature of the study, single-school setting, and lack of long-term follow-up limit generalizability.

identified_tools.name: Intelligent Tutoring System (ITS)
identified_tools.description: An AI-supported tutoring system that provides instructional guidance and may adapt content or feedback based on learner performance.
identified_tools.use_case: Used with Grade 7 gifted students in Thailand learning Measurement and Geometry at Khon Kaen University Demonstration School; 78 students were randomly assigned to use an ITS with automated real-time feedback (n=39) or the same ITS without feedback (n=39). The system used open-ended diagnostic assessment and decision-tree-based SLO classification to personalize instruction; the comparison condition was the identical system with feedback disabled.

findings.finding_summary: Students using the ITS with automated real-time feedback showed greater improvement in SLO-based mathematics performance than students using the same system without feedback. Mean scores increased from 1.90 to 3.54 (SD=0.85) in the feedback group versus 1.90 to 2.85 (SD=1.27) in the no-feedback group; the Time × Group interaction was significant (F=9.240, p=.003, partial eta-squared=.108).
findings.measure: SLO-based conceptual structure mathematics score on open-ended Measurement and Geometry assessment

findings.finding_summary: At post-test, the ITS with feedback group significantly outperformed the no-feedback group on SLO performance, after no baseline difference at pre-test. The post-test pairwise comparison was significant (t=2.829, p=.006, partial eta-squared=.095).

Relative gain in SLO-based mathematical proficiency was higher for students receiving automated feedback. The feedback group reached 84.83% progression (SD=25.57; Advanced level) versus 61.54% (SD=37.40; Medium level) in the no-feedback group, a difference of 23.29 percentage points; the between-group comparison was significant (t=3.21, p=0.001).
findings.measure: Relative Gain Score / progression percentage in SLO-based mathematical proficiency

findings.finding_summary: Post-intervention proficiency-level distribution favored the ITS with feedback group. In the feedback condition, 74.4% of students reached the Advanced level, compared with 43.6% in the no-feedback condition.
findings.measure: Distribution of post-intervention SLO proficiency levels

quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed randomized controlled trial with a control group and pretest-posttest design, but it has notable concerns including a small pilot sample, single-site implementation, gifted-only participants, and limited reporting on implementation fidelity and duration.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports a positive and educationally meaningful effect size of 0.73, with statistically significant improvements favoring the ITS with real-time feedback over the control condition.
